coverage_rule: The complete catalog and source browser do not establish page or API parity. A page is ported when every catalog example of it has a native adaptation with its events and bindings, or a recorded reason (not-applicable, with the Windows-only API) why it cannot; otherwise it is partial. Runtime load tests establish constructibility; only named interaction tests establish their bounded behaviors; rendering parity against Windows is a separate check.

AccessibilityColorContrast.notes: The catalog has no sample definition for the page; the page itself is ported with the code behind of AccessibilityColorContrastPage.xaml.cs and the gallery's InlineColorPicker in Rust (accessibility_samples.rs, the calculation in contrast.rs): the texts, the text and background pickers (Black and White), RecalculateContrastRatio with the source's rounding (21:1, 4.48:1) and SetCheckState of the three checks, and the preview's background, texts and shapes (the source's x:Bind of the pickers' ColorBrush). Each InlineColorPicker is its composition: the header, a SplitButton with the color preview whose flyout holds the color picker (Picker_ColorChanged, PickerFlyout_Opened), and the hex box (ColorHex_TextChanged, other text ignored). WinUI's inline ColorPicker is not a FerroUI control: the flyout's picker is a ColorView, as on the ColorPicker page, so the page is partial. ThemeResource is DynamicResource and GalleryTileGridStyle is a Border with the card brushes.

AccessibilityKeyboard.notes: All six source examples, with the page's texts and the handlers of AccessibilityKeyboardPage.xaml.cs in Rust (accessibility_samples.rs): the automatic tab order (the XAML order without the text and the disabled button), the manual tab order with TabIndex 1 to 3 and the button that is not a tab stop, the list whose arrow keys move within it (WinUI's ListView is FerroUI's ListBox), the potato buttons with XYFocusKeyboardNavigation Enabled (XYFocus.NavigationModes Enabled), the accelerators Ctrl+R, Ctrl+B and Ctrl+G with their AcceleratorKeys and MakeRedButton_Click, MakeBlueButton_Click and MakeChartreuseButton_Click (a KeyboardAccelerator is the button's HotKey), and the menu with its access keys (WinUI's MenuBar is FerroUI's Menu). The headings are the theme's text styles with their heading levels. FerroUI has no Key Tips: an access key is the underlined letter of the header, so Cut (X) and Paste (V), whose keys are not letters of their text, have no access key (AutomationProperties.AccessKey keeps every source key for assistive technology), and FerroUI does not add a button's accelerator to its tooltip as WinUI does: the page is partial.

AccessibilityScreenReader.notes: All eleven source examples with the page's texts (the page has no code-behind upstream; accessibility_samples.rs sets the source's grapes.jpg and treetops.jpg): the name from a button's content, the names from the text boxes' headers and placeholders, the named list and image, LabeledBy, the description and help text, PositionInSet and SizeOfSet of the three buttons beside the list labeled by its text, the decorative image in the Raw view, the navigation, search and main landmarks, the headings of levels 1 to 3, and the groups named for their context. The headings are the theme's text styles with their heading levels; WinUI's ListView is FerroUI's ListBox, StackPanels with padding, background and corners are Borders, and the x:Bind of an element (LabeledBy) is a Binding of the element by name. FerroUI's TextBox has no Header: each header is a TextBlock above its box that labels it (LabeledBy, in the Raw view). FerroUI's automation has no FullDescription (the visible description is the check box's HelpText) and no Custom landmark with a LocalizedLandmarkType (the Current viewers sidebar is a named Region): the page is partial. Screen-reader output itself is not verified by the tests.

AppBarButton.notes: All six source examples use native CommandBarButton (WinUI's AppBarButton) with AppBarButton_Click of AppBarButtonPage.xaml.cs in Rust: the symbol, font and path icons (the source's Content of the path icon is the Icon, which the template presents), the KeyboardAccelerator Ctrl+S as the HotKey, and the flyout with its text box; the outputs are polite live regions for UIHelper.AnnounceActionForAccessibility. The bitmap icon is BitmapIcon (ferroui-controls-icons) with the source's Slices2.png, drawn in the foreground's single color. The symbol glyphs need the platform's symbol font.

AutoSuggestBox.notes: Both source examples use native AutoSuggestBox with the handlers of AutoSuggestBoxPage.xaml.cs in Rust (control_samples.rs): AutoSuggestBox_TextChanged filters the source's 97 cats by every word of the text a user types (No results found when none matches) and AutoSuggestBox_SuggestionChosen writes the chosen cat; Control2_TextChanged, Control2_SuggestionChosen and Control2_QuerySubmitted search the gallery's controls by every word of their title, prefix matches first, and show the chosen or the first control's image, title and subtitle. The suggestions are the controls' titles (the ToString of ControlInfoDataItem), mapped back to their catalog entries, and case is ignored by Unicode lowercase instead of CurrentCultureIgnoreCase. The search box's UpdateTextOnSelect is False: as in the source, only Control2_SuggestionChosen puts a control's title in the box, so a chosen No results found keeps the text. The output is the gallery's OutputTextBlockStyle, the title its BaseTextBlockStyle (semibold) and WrapWholeWords is WrapWithOverflow.

Binding.notes: All seven source examples with the code behind of BindingPage.xaml.cs in Rust (binding_samples.rs): the OneWay and TwoWay x:Bind between the text boxes (UpdateSourceTrigger PropertyChanged), the x:Bind of a text box's text through a converter (emptyStringToVisibilityConverter is StringConverters.IsNotNullOrEmpty, Visibility is IsVisible), and the detail panel's DataContext x:Bind of the list's SelectedItem, all compiled by the x:Bind core. A native page has no x:Class, so the x:Bind of the page's own members is its code behind in Rust: GreetingMessage is set once (OneTime), FormatDate(DatePickerControl.SelectedDate) follows the picker, and ExampleViewModel is the page's DataContext, read with {Binding} over the markup types ExampleViewModel and ListDetailItem (whose values do not change, so they raise no property changes; TargetNullValue as the source's, whose NullString is empty, not null). FerroUI has no ListView: the list is a ListBox. The Headers are composed and AppBarSeparator is CommandBarSeparator.

Border.notes: The source example uses native Border with the handlers of BorderPage.xaml.cs in Rust: ThicknessSlider_ValueChanged sets the uniform thickness, BGRadioButton_Checked the background (Green, Yellow, Blue, White) and RadioButton_Checked the border brush (DarkGreen, Gold, DarkBlue, White). FerroUI's Slider has no Header (composed) and no StepFrequency or SnapsTo: the steps of 1 of the source are TickFrequency 1 with IsSnapToTickEnabled, the same values. The slider's IsFocusEngagementEnabled is the gamepad focus engagement of Xbox, which FerroUI does not have (not applicable).

The Disable option is the source's OneWay x:Bind of IsChecked, negated by the BoolConverters.Not converter, because the x:Bind core has no member Value on a nullable boolean for the source's IsChecked.Value.Equals(x:False). ComboBox.notes: All three source examples use native ComboBox with ColorComboBox_SelectionChanged and Combo3_Loaded of ComboBoxPage.xaml.cs in Rust: the color rectangle, the font list (FontHelper.Fonts as their names, the output's font following the selection in Rust instead of the x:Bind of FontItem.Font through a cast), and the editable font sizes (the source's FontSizes) with the source's OneWay x:Bind of SelectedValue to the output's font size. Header is composed. Missing: FerroUI's ComboBox has no TextSubmitted event and there is no ContentDialog, so Combo3_TextSubmitted (accepting a typed size between 8 and 100, or reverting the text and showing the dialog) is not ported and the page stays partial.

CommandBar.notes: The source example uses native CommandBar with the code behind of CommandBarPage.xaml.cs in Rust: OnElementClicked (the clicked command's label), Open and Close (IsOpen with IsSticky), AddSecondaryCommands_Click (four buttons and a separator while Settings is alone) and RemoveSecondaryCommands, and the KeyboardAccelerators of the constructor and the markup as HotKeys (Ctrl+A, Ctrl+E, F4, Ctrl+I; Ctrl+N, Delete, Ctrl+Subtract, Ctrl+Add). The MultipleButtons property feeds the source viewer's substitutions only, and the gallery creates the page anew instead of OnNavigatingFrom. FerroUI's CommandBar has no closed display mode: its buttons keep their labels while it is closed. The symbol glyphs need the platform's symbol font.

CustomUserControls.notes: All three source examples with the page's texts and the custom controls of the page in Rust (custom_controls.rs): CounterControl (Count and Mode styled properties, OnApplyTemplate with its ActionButton and CountText parts, UpdateUI and UpdateButtonText) in its two modes, ValidatedPasswordBox (Password, IsValid, MinLength, Header and PlaceholderText, OnApplyTemplate and UpdateValidationMessages with the colors of the theme) above the Submit button that its IsValid enables (the source's OneWay x:Bind), and the UserControl TemperatureConverterControl with HasText and Button_Click. The counter's default style (DefaultStyleKey) is the page's control theme of CounterControl.xaml; the template of ValidatedPasswordBox.xaml is built in Rust (FuncControlTemplate), because a TextBox inside a ControlTemplate of run-time loaded markup does not get its own template part PART_TextPresenter when it is laid out (a framework defect, found by validated_password_box_lays_out_its_template_in_a_window); a native page has no XAML namespace of its own types, so the sample creates the controls in their hosts. The validation lines are a panel of icon and text lines, the source's RichTextBlock of InlineUIContainers. FerroUI has no PasswordBox: the template's password box is a TextBox with a PasswordChar, so the page is partial.

DatePicker.notes: Both source examples use native DatePicker: the picker with its header (composed above it), and the picker with the formatted day and hidden year with OnNavigatedTo of DatePickerPage.xaml.cs in Rust (the date two months from now, within the years from now to five years from now; WinUI's Date is the SelectedDate). FerroUI's DayFormat is a .NET date format: WinUI's {day.integer} ({dayofweek.abbreviated}) is d (ddd).

DropDownButton.notes: Both source examples use native DropDownButton with a MenuFlyout placed BottomEdgeAlignedLeft: the text button and the icon button, with the source's FontIcon glyphs on the button and on the items. Expander.notes: Both source examples use native Expander: the text header and content with ExpandDirectionComboBox_SelectionChanged of ExpanderPage.xaml.cs in Rust (Down from the top, Up from the bottom), and the centered header over left-aligned content (HorizontalContentAlignment Left, Padding 0). Flyout.notes: The source example uses native Button.Flyout with DeleteConfirmation_Click of FlyoutPage.xaml.cs in Rust: the confirmation hides the flyout. The message's BaseTextBlockStyle is its semibold weight; the page's SharedFlyout resource is used by no example and is left out.

Geometry.notes: The source example with the code behind of GeometryPage.xaml.cs in Rust (shape_samples.rs): the header image of the page's theme (the source's Geometry.dark.png for the Default theme and Geometry.light.png for Light, its ThemeDictionaries), the three tip buttons of ShowGeometryButtonClick1 to 3, and CopyOverlayResourceToClipboardButton_Click and CopyControlResourceToClipboardButton_Click, which put the resource's name on the window's clipboard (the gallery's CopyButton is a Button with its glyph, its feedback a polite live region). The corner radius table keeps the source's rows; the radii are their values (8 and 4), CaptionTextBlockStyle is 12, the card styles are Borders with the card brushes and the selectable style names are SelectableTextBlocks (no IsTextSelectionEnabled on TextBlock). Each tip is the TeachingTip of ferroui-controls-teaching-tip, whose IsOpen the click toggles. The glyphs need the platform's symbol font.

Grid.notes: The source example uses native Grid with the source's OneWay x:Bind of ColumnSpacing, RowSpacing and the red rectangle's Grid.Column and Grid.Row to the sliders; the binding converts the values instead of the source's (x:Int32) casts, which the x:Bind core makes a type test. HyperlinkButton.notes: Both source examples use native HyperlinkButton: NavigateUri opens the Microsoft home page through the launcher of the top level, with the Disable option as the source's OneWay x:Bind of IsChecked negated by the BoolConverters.Not converter instead of IsChecked.Value.Equals(x:False); GoToHyperlinkButton_Click navigates the gallery to the ToggleButton page, as App.MainWindow.Navigate does in the source (examples::GALLERY_LINKS, wired by the gallery).

IconElement.notes: All six source examples with MonochromeButton_CheckedChanged of IconElementPage.xaml.cs in Rust (brush_samples.rs): the FontIcon with the source's font family and glyph, the PathIcon and the SymbolIcon in their buttons use the native icons. The bitmap icon is BitmapIcon and the PNG image icon is ImageIcon (ferroui-controls-icons), with the check box setting ShowAsMonochrome. FerroUI decodes no SVG and the remote SVG of the source is not loaded: its button says so, which is what keeps the page partial. The glyphs need the source's icon fonts.

InfoBar.notes: All three source examples use native InfoBar with the code behind of InfoBarPage.xaml.cs in Rust (control_samples.rs): SeverityComboBox_SelectionChanged (Informational, Success, Warning, Error), MessageComboBox_SelectionChanged (the short and the long message, long at load) and ActionButtonComboBox_SelectionChanged (none, the Action button, the Informational link to the Microsoft home page). The Is Open, Is Icon Visible and Is Closable options keep the source's TwoWay x:Bind, compiled by the x:Bind core. The page has no code-behind upstream. WinUI's X1, Y1, X2 and Y2 are FerroUI's StartPoint and EndPoint: the four point sliders set them in Rust (shape_samples.rs) for the source's TwoWay x:Bind of each coordinate. FerroUI's Slider has no Header (composed) and no StepFrequency or SnapsTo: the steps of 0.5 are TickFrequency with IsSnapToTickEnabled. Canvas.ZIndex is the shared ZIndex; the Rect of RectangleGeometry is written x,y,width,height.

ListView.notes: All ten source examples use native ListBox (FerroUI has no ListView) with the code behind of ListViewPage.xaml.cs in Rust (list_samples.rs): the basic list, which takes the focus when it is loaded; SelectionModeComboBox_SelectionChanged (Single; Multiple as Multiple with Toggle; Extended as Multiple; None as items that are not selected, hit or focused, a class of the page, because FerroUI's SelectionMode has no None); ListView_Drop between and within the two lists with the source's insertion index, the contacts in an in-process data format, and a drag that starts when the pointer pressed on an item moves (DragItemsStarting); the grouped contacts after their group headers in one list, the headers not selectable; OnFilterChanged with Remove_NonMatching, AddBack_Contacts and the count in a polite live region (UIHelper.AnnounceActionForAccessibility); the inverted list with AddItemToEnd and MessageReceived, which keeps its last item in view; the images of CustomDataObject; ContactDeleteMenuItem_Click of the items' context menu; the scroll position of ListViewPersistenceHelper (the key of the first visible item and the offset in it), saved and restored; and ScrollIntoView with the Default and Leading alignments. The contacts of Contacts.txt are a table, x:Bind in the templates is {Binding} over markup types and WinUI's StackPanel with a background, padding and corners is a Border. FerroUI has no grouping (CollectionViewSource, GroupStyle) and no sticky group headers (the Sticky Headers switch changes nothing), no IsTextTrimmed on TextBlock (TextBlock_IsTextTrimmedChanged does not set the description's tooltip), no ItemsUpdatingScrollMode and no check boxes of the Multiple mode, so the page is partial.

MenuBar.notes: All three source examples use native Menu (WinUI's MenuBar; MenuBarItem.Title is the Header of a top MenuItem) with OnElementClicked of MenuBarPage.xaml.cs in Rust (the first letter of the item's name picks the output): the simple bar, the bar whose KeyboardAccelerators are HotKeys shown as InputGestures, and the bar with a submenu, separators and two radio groups (RadioMenuFlyoutItem is a MenuItem with the ToggleType Radio).

MenuFlyout.notes: All seven source examples use native MenuFlyout with MenuFlyoutItem_Click and SplitMenuFlyoutItem_Click of MenuFlyoutPage.xaml.cs in Rust: the sort menu of a compact CommandBarButton (the Tag of the item), the check items and separator, the cascading menus, the icons (FontIcon and SymbolIcon), the KeyboardAccelerators as HotKeys shown as InputGestures with the source's fonts, and the radio groups. WinUI's MenuFlyoutItem is MenuItem (Text is Header); ToggleMenuFlyoutItem and RadioMenuFlyoutItem are MenuItems with the ToggleType CheckBox and Radio. Save and Share are the SplitMenuFlyoutItem of ferroui-controls-split-menu, whose primary part raises SplitMenuFlyoutItem_Click. The glyphs need the platform's symbol font.

NumberBox.notes: All three source examples use native NumberBox with the code behind of NumberBoxPage.xaml.cs in Rust: the expression box, the spin button box with SpinButtonPlacementGroup_SelectionChanged (Inline, Compact; as in the source the box keeps its markup placement until the selection changes), and SetNumberBoxNumberFormatter, a formatter of two fraction digits that rounds half up to 0.25 (DecimalFormatter with an IncrementNumberRounder). FerroUI's Frame has no navigation transitions (ContentTransitions with a NavigationThemeTransition, the NavigationTransitionInfo of Navigate): the navigation is not animated and the mode changes nothing, so the page is partial.

ScrollViewer.notes: The source example uses native ScrollViewer with the source's cliff.jpg and the code behind of ScrollViewerPage.xaml.cs in Rust (scroll_samples.rs): the constructor's ZoomToFactor(4) (once the scroll viewer is first loaded, when it has its presenter), ZoomModeComboBox_SelectionChanged (the zoom mode, the slider enabled only with zooming, the factor 2 otherwise), ZoomSlider_ValueChanged (ChangeView), ScrollViewerControl_ViewChanged (the slider follows a change of ZoomFactor) and the four scroll mode and bar visibility handlers; the slider keeps the source's OneWay x:Bind of MinZoomFactor and MaxZoomFactor (its Header is composed). The ThemeShadow is a resource set as the Shadow, as the templates of the WinUI theme share theirs; OverlayCornerRadius is its value, 8. Rendering against Windows captures remains pending.

examples.notes: ThemeShadow on a Border, its receiver and the Z-translation slider (StepFrequency is TickFrequency with IsSnapToTickEnabled; Header is a composed label).

Acrylic.notes: All three source examples use the native AcrylicBrush over the source's shapes: the theme's AcrylicInAppFillColorDefaultBrush, and the page's CustomAcrylicInAppBrush and CustomAcrylicInAppLuminosity with the source's values, page resources under their keys, changed by AcrylicPage_Loaded, Slider_ValueChanged, ColorSelector_SelectionChanged, FallbackColorSelector_SelectionChanged and LuminositySlider_ValueChanged in Rust. The SolidColorBrush items of the colour boxes and their ColorTemplate are composed items (a swatch and the colour); the handlers map the selected index to the colour. The ThemeDictionaries of the source have only Default, so the brushes are plain resources; the AdaptiveTrigger sizes are the wide ones. The link of the intro to the SystemBackdrops page is text. Rendering against Windows captures remains pending.

examples.notes: The theme resource AcrylicInAppFillColorDefaultBrush (a DynamicResource) over the source's shapes.
TintOpacity, TintColor and FallbackColor of the page's brush from the slider and the two colour boxes, as the C# handlers set them.
TintOpacity and TintLuminosityOpacity of the luminosity brush from its two sliders.

SystemBackdrops.notes: The three "Show window" buttons open the source's sample windows (SampleBuiltInSystemBackdropsWindow and SampleSystemBackdropsWindow with its AllowedBackdrops) as native windows extended into the title bar: Window.SystemBackdrop with MicaBackdrop (Base, BaseAlt) and DesktopAcrylicBackdrop, and MicaController and DesktopAcrylicController (Base, Thin) on the window as their target, with a SystemBackdropConfiguration that follows activation, the theme of the window and high contrast. SetBackdrop resets the previous backdrop and falls back as the C# does where IsSupported is false (Mica is drawn on Windows 11 and macOS, desktop acrylic also where the platform blurs a transparent window); the theme box sets the window's theme and SetNoneBackdropBackground its background. The C# window adds its Activated, Closed and ActualThemeChanged handlers again for every backdrop it sets; they are added once. UIHelper.AnnounceActionForAccessibility is a polite live region, the ComboBox headers are composed labels, the badge logo image of the custom title bar is not shown and TitleBarHelper.ApplySystemThemeToCaptionButtons is left to the decorations of the window, which follow its theme. The platform's drawing of the materials is verified on the hosts, not by these tests.

examples.notes: The built-in window: MicaBackdrop, MicaBackdrop Kind=BaseAlt, DesktopAcrylicBackdrop and none, with the fallbacks of SetBackdrop.
MicaController (Base, BaseAlt) with AddSystemBackdropTarget on the window and SetSystemBackdropConfiguration; disposed when another backdrop is set and when the window closes.
DesktopAcrylicController (Base, Thin) with the same configuration.

TitleBar.notes: All three source examples use the native TitleBar. The configuration example binds Title, Subtitle, IsBackButtonVisible and IsPaneToggleButtonVisible to the options (the source x:Bind to the named options, compiled by the x:Bind core; IsOn is IsChecked of the ToggleSwitch; Header is a composed label). The two "Show window" buttons open the source's sample windows, extended into a tall title bar with Mica: TitleBar.IsDragRegion of the status badge (unset, true, false), its Click, the extra button and RecomputeDragRegions; and the end-to-end window with the back button bound to Frame.CanGoBack, BackRequested, PaneToggleRequested and NavigationView navigation over the gallery's sample pages. ImageIconSource is a PathIconSource and PersonPicture a composed circle with the initials, since FerroUI has neither (G2). TitleBar_LayoutUpdated (TitleBarHelper.ApplySystemThemeToCaptionButtons) is left to the decorations of the window; the link of the intro to the AppWindowTitleBar page is text. Dragging the window is verified on the hosts, not by these tests.

examples.notes: Title, subtitle and the two button visibilities bound to the options; the icon, the search box and the initials in the bar.
TitleBarDragRegionsWindow: SetIsDragRegion and ClearValue of the badge, the badge's Click, the extra button inserted and removed, RecomputeDragRegions.
TitleBarWindow: the NavigationView selection navigates the frame and sets the header; the back button follows CanGoBack; BackRequested goes back and PaneToggleRequested opens and closes the pane.

RichEditBox.notes: The simple editor, the custom context menu command and the formatting editor use the native RichEditBox and its text object model: bold and italic toggles, font colors from the Rectangle of the clicked button with the TextChanged rule for new text, find with FindText highlighting and its focus handlers, and RTF open/save through the storage provider of the window. The context menu is the MenuFlyout of the WinUI theme (no CommandBarFlyout or touch SelectionFlyout); Share is a MenuItem in place of StandardUICommand. The two math examples need the math mode of the Windows RichEdit control and are recorded as not applicable, with their explanation and a diagnostic on the page. Segoe glyphs of the toolbar, exact visuals and host accessibility remain pending.

examples.notes: A native RichEditBox with the source automation name; typing, deletion and the theme's context menu are the control's own.

Menu_Opening is ported to the Opening event of the box's context menu (subscribed while the box has one, the Loaded/Unloaded pair): the Share command is added when the menu opens for REBCustom, once rather than at every opening, and removed when the shared menu of the theme opens for another editor. The menu is a MenuFlyout, not a CommandBarFlyout, and Share is a MenuItem with the label of StandardUICommandKind.Share and no icon or action. The SelectionFlyout half is missing: FerroUI has no selection flyout (CommandBarFlyout is phase G2).

All handlers are ported: BoldButton/ItalicButton toggle the selection, ColorButton takes the color of the Rectangle in the clicked button, closes the flyout, focuses the editor and becomes the color of new text (Editor_TextChanged); FindBoxHighlightMatches/FindBoxRemoveHighlights use FindText with the system highlight colors on GotFocus, LostFocus and text changes, and Editor_GotFocus clears the highlight background. Open/Save use the storage provider of the window (an .rtf filter, the documents folder, import_rtf/export_rtf) in place of the Windows App SDK pickers; a failure is reported in a text block below the editor instead of a MessageDialog. VariableSizedWrapGrid is a three-column UniformGrid.

examples.reason: TextDocument.SetMathMode(RichEditMathMode.MathOnly) is the math engine of the Windows RichEdit control (msftedit), a Windows-only API; the FerroUI editor has no math mode.
examples.notes: The page keeps the explanation and an editor without math mode, with a visible diagnostic.

examples.reason: ITextDocument.SetMathML and GetMathML need the math mode of the Windows RichEdit control (msftedit), a Windows-only API.
examples.notes: The page keeps the explanation, the editor, the MathML code view with its empty-content text and a disabled Set sample formula button, with a visible diagnostic.

RichTextBlock.notes: All four examples use the native RichTextBlock: paragraphs with formatted runs and a hyperlink, SelectionHighlightColor, OverflowContentTarget through two RichTextBlockOverflow columns, and a TextHighlighter whose color follows the ComboBox selection over the source range 28+11. The overflow targets keep the source x:Bind of the elements; mixed text content is written as explicit Runs; the ComboBox header is composed. Exact text layout, fonts and host accessibility remain pending.

examples.notes: A native RichTextBlock with the source paragraph.
SelectionHighlightColor Green over the source paragraphs, with the bold italic run and the hyperlink; selection is the control's own.
The justified RichTextBlock flows into two linked RichTextBlockOverflow columns through the source x:Bind of the elements.

HighlightColorCombobox_SelectionChanged in Rust: the color named by the selected item replaces the TextHighlighter of characters 28 to 39; the initially selected Yellow item applies on load as in the source.

ItemsRepeater.notes: All six catalog examples (and the nested repeaters of the source page, which has no sample definition of its own) use the native ItemsRepeater of ferroui-controls-repeater with the layouts, element factories and selectors of the port; the Gallery layouts ActivityFeedLayout and VariedImageSizeLayout are Rust VirtualizingLayouts; x:Bind becomes {Binding} over markup types and the C# handlers are Rust. Four examples are ported; the animated scrolling and content-heavy examples miss the accessibility announcements and the key-index mapping of their custom source. ThemeResource becomes DynamicResource; text styles are written as their sizes and weights. Rendering and host accessibility acceptance remain pending.

examples.notes: Native ItemsRepeater over an observable list of Bar models: Add Item and Remove Item (disabled at zero items) and the layout choice set the vertical StackLayout, horizontal StackLayout or UniformGridLayout with the HorizontalBar, VerticalBar or Circular template and the MaxWidth of the source handler. The templates bind the Bar sizes with {Binding} (x:Bind). System.Random is a seeded generator; the code substitutions of the source viewer are not updated by the options.

ItemsRepeaterScrollHost and ScrollViewer around a repeater of 500 numbers; MyDataTemplateSelector is a native IDataTemplateSelector (even Normal, odd Accent); the Gallery ActivityFeedLayout is ported to a Rust VirtualizingLayout (rows of two narrow and one wide tile, virtualized by rows, its state per context), and the option switches to the UniformGridLayout of the source.

FlowLayout over 500 items with the orientation, line alignment, minimum item spacing and line spacing options; ElementPrepared and ElementClearing keep the realized elements and update the count once per dispatcher turn (TryEnqueue). ScrollMode has no FerroUI counterpart: the orientation sets the scroll bar visibilities, a disabled scroll bar disabling scrolling. Header becomes a label.

The mixed list of numbers and text in a UniformGridLayout; StringOrIntTemplateSelector is a native IDataTemplateSelector choosing IntDataTemplate or StringDataTemplate by the type of the item. HeaderTextBlockStyle is written as its size and weight.

Buttons of the 20 colours: a click colours the rectangle and names the selected button; GotFocus remembers the index and centres the item; GettingFocus returns focus from outside to that item; Home and End reach the first and the last item. Adapted: the composition ExpressionAnimation on the scroll manipulation property set becomes a scale set from the scroll offset after each layout pass and scroll change (same expression, about the item centre); StartBringIntoView with VerticalAlignmentRatio 0.5 becomes a scroll offset that centres the item, without the animation. Pending: the accessibility announcement of UIHelper.AnnounceActionForAccessibility (no notification event on FerroUI automation peers).

The Gallery VariedImageSizeLayout is ported to a Rust VirtualizingLayout (columns of 200, the lowest column first, bounds cached until the items change); 1000 generated recipes (seeded generator) bound with {Binding} over the Recipe markup type; the ingredient filter (ignoring case) and the two sort orders replace the items. Pending: the IKeyIndexMapping of the custom MyItemsSource (an observable list is replaced instead) and the automation notification of the result count.

LayoutPanel.notes: The catalog example uses the native LayoutPanel with its border, corner radius and padding around the layout; the FeaturedTileLayout of the source (Samples/LayoutPanel/FeaturedTileLayout.cs) is a Rust NonVirtualizingLayout, and the options switch to a vertical StackLayout and set the spacing of both, as the C# handlers do. Header becomes a label, ThemeResource becomes DynamicResource. Rendering and host accessibility acceptance remain pending.

examples.notes: The nine children arranged by the ported FeaturedTileLayout (the first spanning the width, then rows of two columns as high as their taller child), the layout choice (featured tile or vertical stack) and the spacing slider, with the handlers of the source.

InkCanvas.notes: All three source examples use the native InkCanvas, InkPresenter and InkToolbar of ferroui-controls-inking with the handlers of InkCanvasPage.xaml.cs in Rust: input devices, ink colour, stroke width, inking enabled and clear; the toolbar's available tools, active tool in both directions, button flyout placement and clear; save, clear and restore with the source's status messages. Header is composed with a label, IsOn maps to IsChecked, TargetInkCanvas (x:Bind of an element) is set in Rust, and the saved strokes are the bytes of InkStrokeContainer::save in memory instead of SaveAsync into an InMemoryRandomAccessStream. Tests drive the presenter with ink pointer input; routed pointer input of a window, the toolbar's WinUI styles (Themes/WinUI.xaml of the crate), rendering and screen-reader acceptance are not established by them.

examples.notes: The pen, mouse and touch options set InkPresenter.InputDeviceTypes; the colour and width options update the default drawing attributes (CopyDefaultDrawingAttributes/UpdateDefaultDrawingAttributes); the toggle sets IsInputEnabled; Clear drawing clears the stroke container. The substitutions of the source code view stay in the catalog viewer.

An InkToolbar with InitialControls None and the four source buttons targets its canvas. The show options hide and show the pencil, highlighter and eraser (falling back to the ballpoint pen), the active-tool option selects the tool and follows ActiveToolChanged, the placement option sets ButtonFlyoutPlacement, and Clear drawing clears the canvas, with the source's reentrancy guard. The toolbar draws with its WinUI styles only where the application includes Themes/WinUI.xaml of ferroui-controls-inking.

Save, clear and restore keep the source's stroke count, restore enabling and status messages; StrokesCollected and StrokesErased update the count. InkStrokeContainer::save and load (the portable ink format of the crate, synchronously in memory) replace SaveAsync and LoadAsync with an InMemoryRandomAccessStream.

Chart.notes: The seven examples of the source (Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Charts) map onto the native CartesianChart of ferroui-controls-livecharts with the data and the option handlers of ChartPage.xaml.cs in Rust: Chart is CartesianChart, CategoryAxis/LinearAxis are Axis (labels from the source arrays), LineSeries/AreaSeries/BarSeries are LineSeries/AreaSeries/ColumnSeries (RowSeries when horizontal), ShowLegend is LegendPosition, ShowDataMarkers is GeometrySize, StrokeDashStyle is a dash array, and the DateTimeAxis is an axis over the days of its range with day labels and the ticks of the interval type. Not available in the native chart, and recorded per example: LegendTitle, tick marks and axis line/tick brushes, marker shapes and per-point label and marker overrides, a marker brush apart from the area fill. Rendering parity with WinUI and screen-reader acceptance are not established.

examples.notes: A line series of the six profits over the month labels with the legend toggle (LegendPosition Top or Hidden). The legend has no title (LegendTitle "Profit"): the native legend lists the series names only.

A column series of units sold per region. Orientation switches the series between column and row (the categories move to the vertical axis); SortKey (data order or value) and SortOrder reorder the points and the category labels, which the source's CategoryAxis sorts itself.

Grid lines None/Major/Minor set the separator lines of the visitors axis (Minor adds the separators at every 10), the axes toggle sets IsVisible of both axes and the tick-labels toggle hides their labels with a transparent label colour. Missing: tick marks (the ShowTickMarks option is not shown) and the AxisLineBrush, TickBrush and GridLineMinorBrush of the source.

The forecast area, the actual columns with data labels and the dashed target line with the source colours and thickness; the three check boxes set IsVisible of each series. Missing: the Diamond marker shape and a DataMarkerBrush apart from the fill (the markers are circles in the stroke colour).

The daily visits line with markers and data labels; dash style (in multiples of the thickness), thickness, data markers and data labels options. Missing: marker shapes (the Marker shape option is not shown) and the Peak label and marker overrides of HighlightPeakVisits (DataLabelOverrides and DataMarkerOverrides).

CreateTimeSeriesChart in Rust: the temperature area over a date axis from 2026-07-27 to 2026-09-07 (an axis over its 42 days, labelled per day). Tick interval Auto/Day/Week/Month sets the separators (the chart's own step, every day, every week, the first day of each month); the label formats month day, month.abbreviated day and shortdate are formatted in en-US.

Add sample appends the next incoming response time, keeps the eight most recent values and updates the series (the chart redraws) and the summary text, as the source's ResponseTimes and LiveSeriesSummary do.

ItemsView.notes: G1 (#418) found no WinUI ItemsView on main: ferroui-controls-repeater has the ItemsRepeater, LinedFlowLayout and SelectionModel, but not ItemsView or ItemContainer (ferroui_controls::ItemsView in items_source.rs is an unrelated view of items). The three examples need its container selection modes, ItemInvoked and the ScrollView it hosts; the control is G2 work.

SystemBackdropElement.notes: G1 (#418) found no SystemBackdropElement on main: the system backdrop of an element exists only inside the framework (ElementSystemBackdrop of the menu flyout presenter, crate-private). The catalog has no sample definition for the page; the element is G2 work.

MediaPlayerElement.notes: Both source compositions use native portable MediaPlayerElement. The existing bundled Sintel H.264/AAC excerpt replaces unbundled WMV files. Load, file picker, autoplay, compact transport and full-window are wired in Rust. Desktop backend acceptance is recorded separately.

CaptureElementPreview.notes: The source preview uses CameraPreview through CameraCaptureUI, with explicit start/stop and no acquisition on page construction. The added capture actions return owned photos and optional silent video; recording remains disabled on providers that do not advertise it.

Sound.notes: The seven two-dimensional UI sound actions play application-owned PCM cues through the native portable MediaPlayer. The toggle and volume operate that player. SpatialAudioMode is explicitly not applicable: it is a Windows UI service without a portable provider contract.
